summary: Modular monolith Spring Boot on On-premise servers with PostgreSQL as the database in India; front end: React + Vite.

architecture_rationale.text: One Spring Boot deployable split into internal modules: clear boundaries for 4 engineers without the operational cost of microservices. Microservices rejected: 4 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: A client-rendered app behind login needs no server rendering. Fit for this project: well suited to internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the team would have to learn Python.
Close runner-up: the team would have to learn TypeScript; learning curve 4/5 for a intermediate team; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).

tradeoffs: Client-rendered: no SEO for public pages.
The team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript.

backend.justification: Mature transaction management and Spring Security for regulated domains. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Java; strong security, which you rated 5/5; mature transaction management for money/ledger flows.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the team would have to learn C#; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes Java).
Excluded: AWS Lambda + API Gateway is a managed cloud service and cannot run air-gapped (infrastructure.deployment_model).

tradeoffs: Slower start-up and more memory than Go/Node.
Learning curve 4/5 for a intermediate team.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: ACID transactions keep related records consistent; strong security, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects; the team already writes SQL.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on priorities.security (strong security, which you rated 5/5).
Lower overall fit: SQL Server licensing and tooling only pay off for .NET teams or existing SQL Server estates; the chosen option wins on team.languages (the team already writes SQL).
Excluded: Cloud Firestore is a managed cloud service and cannot run air-gapped (infrastructure.deployment_model).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.choice: On-premise servers (Docker Compose; k3s for HA)
hosting.justification: Runs entirely on servers you control.

alternatives.why_not: Excluded: Azure App Service is a managed cloud service and cannot run air-gapped (infrastructure.deployment_model).

tradeoffs: Hardware, power, backups and patching are yours (capex not in the estimate).
A lot of infrastructure to operate.

supporting.justification: Runs inside your network; no external identity service.

alternatives.why_not: Keycloak centralises accounts for future apps.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (approval e-mails) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.choice: PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector + GIN, pg_trgm for typos)
supporting.justification: At 1200 users and ~2.3 GB the database's own search is fast enough, transactional and needs no sync pipeline.

alternatives.why_not: Better typo tolerance and ranking, but another service to keep in sync; move to it if search becomes core.

supporting.justification: Code, pipelines and the container registry all live inside the air-gapped network.
Metrics, dashboards and logs without any external SaaS.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L1: ~1200 users, ~200 peak concurrent, ~40 req/s at peak, ~2.3 GB stored
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees and payment-gateway transaction fees
On-premise: hardware purchase (capex) is excluded; figure covers power, licences and maintenance contracts only

warnings.message: Online payments need an external payment gateway, which an air-gapped network cannot reach. Payments were removed from the recommendation; handle them in a separate, connected system.
auth=social needs external identity/SMS providers; an air-gapped network cannot reach them. Replaced with local accounts in Keycloak.
The web choice (React + Vite (SPA)) needs JavaScript/TypeScript, which the team does not list; budget ramp-up time or a hire. It still scored best once constraints and other priorities were weighed.

Priorities not given for cost, time_to_market, scalability, performance, maintainability; defaulted to 3.
scale.data_volume_gb_12_months not given; estimated 2.3 GB (2 MB per user).
